runs.question: How much does block payload size affect block propagation time on mainnet?
runs.answer:
Here's the analysis of block payload size vs propagation time on mainnet over the past 7 days:

**Answer: The effect is measurable but modest.** A 5–6× increase in block size (~62KB → ~400KB) results in only ~20–30% longer propagation.

| Size Bucket | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | Observations |
|------------|---------|---------|------------|
| 50–75 KB   | 1,581   | 3,075   | 328,583 |
| 75–100 KB  | 1,637   | 3,109   | 423,947 |
| 100–125 KB | 1,668   | 3,170   | 621,074 |
| 125–150 KB | 1,691   | 3,186   | 887,738 |
| 150–175 KB | 1,747   | 3,266   | 995,913 |
| 175–200 KB | 1,773   | 3,281   | 991,241 |
| 200–250 KB | 1,809   | 3,343   | 1,469,553 |
| 250–300 KB | 1,874   | 3,399   | 808,972 |
| 300+ KB    | 1,952   | 3,477   | 786,873 |

- **Pearson r = 0.16**, **Spearman ρ = 0.20** — significant but weak correlation
- p50 rises from 1,581 → 1,952 ms (+371 ms / +23%)
- p95 rises from 3,075 → 3,477 ms (+402 ms / +13%)

**Key takeaway:** Block payload size is not a dominant factor in propagation latency. Network topology, geographic distance, and client implementation matter far more. Even a ~800 KB block propagates within ~2 seconds at the median and ~3.5 seconds at p95.

runs.question: Around the 3rd-4th of December 2025, MEV relay circuit breakers reportedly tripped on mainnet and relay-delivered blocks collapsed for a while. Find the actual window and quantify how bad it got.
runs.answer:
Here are the findings:

**Incident window:** Dec 4, 2025, **03:00–05:00 UTC**, with the nadir at **03:30–04:00 UTC**.

**How bad it got:**

| Window | MEV slots | Total slots | MEV % |
|--------|-----------|-------------|-------|
| Normal baseline (Dec 2) | 6,590 | 7,144 | **92.2%** |
| Precursor (Dec 3 22:00–Dec 4 03:00) | 1,256 | 1,422 | **88.3%** |
| Declining (03:00–03:28) | 59 | 105 | **56.2%** |
| **Severe (03:28–05:00)** | **95** | **328** | **29.0%** |
| Nadir (03:30–04:00) | 18 | 104 | **17.3%** |
| Recovery (05:00–07:00) | 454 | 539 | **84.2%** |

Every major relay was affected — Ultra Sound, Titan, BloXroute, Flashbots, Aestus, Agnostic Gnosis, EthGas all dropped from ~85–95% slot coverage to near-zero. During the nadir, only 18 of 104 canonical slots (17.3%) had any MEV-delivered block.

Canonical slot fill also suffered: only 69–75% of expected slots had blocks (vs ~96% normally), implying ~25% of slots were completely missed during the worst hour. Transaction throughput fell from ~80k/hr to ~50k/hr. Recovery was essentially complete by 06:00 UTC.

**Chart:** [MEV-delivered slots % collapsed to ~17%](http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/068c10dbde37/756a1ff4-ebdb-4a28-9805-84ef273874de/mev_circuit_breaker_dec4_2025.png)

runs.question: Around the 3rd-4th of December 2025, MEV relay circuit breakers reportedly tripped on mainnet and relay-delivered blocks collapsed for a while. Find the actual window and quantify how bad it got.
runs.answer:
Here's what the data reveals:

**Incident window:** `2025-12-03 22:00 UTC` to `2025-12-04 10:00 UTC` (~12 hours), with the worst collapse `2025-12-04 03:00–04:59 UTC`.

**Severity quantification:**

| Hour (UTC) | Total blocks | MEV-relayed | MEV % | Missed slots |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dec 3 20:00 | 299 | 271 | **90.6%** | 1 |
| Dec 3 21:00 | 288 | 266 | **92.4%** | 11 |
| Dec 3 22:00 | 281 | 240 | **85.4%** | 19 |
| Dec 3 23:00 | 287 | 266 | **92.7%** | 13 |
| Dec 4 00:00 | 292 | 264 | **90.4%** | 8 |
| Dec 4 01:00 | 291 | 250 | **85.9%** | 9 |
| Dec 4 02:00 | 290 | 238 | **82.1%** | 10 |
| **Dec 4 03:00** | **224** | **77** | **34.4%** | **77** |
| **Dec 4 04:00** | **240** | **77** | **32.1%** | **62** |
| Dec 4 05:00 | 281 | 212 | **75.4%** | 20 |
| Dec 4 06:00 | 286 | 243 | **85.0%** | 14 |
| Dec 4 07:00 | 283 | 235 | **83.0%** | 17 |
| Dec 4 08:00 | 286 | 239 | **83.6%** | 14 |
| Dec 4 09:00 | 288 | 251 | **87.2%** | 13 |
| Dec 4 10:00 | 294 | 261 | **88.8%** | 7 |

Normal MEV share is ~91–93%. At the trough, it dropped to **32–34%** — a ~3× reduction. Missed slots spiked from a baseline of 1–4/hour to **77** (03:00) and **62** (04:00).

**Per-relay during the trough (03:00–04:59 UTC):**
- Ultra Sound: 44+47 = 91 (vs ~140-160/hr normally)
- BloXroute Max Profit: 35+38 = 73
- Titan Relay: 30+25 = 55
- BloXroute Regulated: 25+26 = 51
- Flashbots: 14+5 = 19 (collapsed hardest)
- Aestus: 8+4 = 12
- Agnostic Gnosis: 7+3 = 10
- EthGas: 3+0 = 3

All relays were hit proportionally — every relay's delivery dropped to roughly 1/3 of normal volume.

**Worst non-MEV streak:** 12 consecutive slots (13166270–13166281, ~4 min) with zero MEV deliveries at `2025-12-04 03:34:23`.

Recovery began around 05:00 UTC and MEV share was back above 85% by 06:00, essentially normal by 12:00 UTC.

Full data saved at `/workspace/mev_collapse.csv`.

runs.answer:
Here are the findings:

## Real Window

The circuit breaker event occurred on **Dec 4, 2025, ~02:00–04:59 UTC**, with the trough at **03:00–04:00 UTC** — shifted later than the "Dec 3rd-4th" reference by about a day.

## Severity

| Metric | Baseline | Trough (03:00–04:00 UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| Total canonical blocks/hr | ~297 | **216–217** |
| MEV-relayed blocks/hr | ~274 | **77** |
| MEV share of blocks | **92.2%** | **35.5%** |
| Locally-built blocks/hr | ~23 | ~140 |
| Missed slots/hr (no block) | ~3 | **~72** |

**Summary**: MEV relay-delivered blocks collapsed by **72%** (274→77/hr), driving a **61.5 percentage point** share loss. ~72 additional slots per hour had no canonical block at all — validators' local fallback also missed the slot deadline. All 8 relays were affected simultaneously.

## Recovery

Fast: **05:00 UTC** → 80.5% MEV share; **07:00 UTC** → fully normalized. Total duration of depressed delivery: ~3 hours, full incident window ~5 hours.

runs.question: On mainnet around December 3rd-4th, 2025, MEV relay circuit breakers were said to have tripped and relay-delivered blocks dropped sharply for a period. Identify the real window and measure the severity of the collapse.
runs.answer:
Here is the full analysis:

**Actual window:** The circuit breakers impacted relay-delivered blocks from **2025-12-04 ~02:50 UTC** through **~04:55 UTC** (~2 hours). The most severe 30-minute trough was **03:10–03:40 UTC** when MEV block delivery nearly halted.

**Evidence (5-minute granularity):**

| Period (Dec 4) | MEV blocks/5min | vs baseline (~21/5min) |
|---|---|---|
| 02:50–02:55 | 15, 13 | begins declining |
| 03:00–03:10 | 12, 11, 5 | steep drop |
| 03:25–03:30 | **1, 0** | **95–100% collapse** |
| 03:35–03:55 | 7, 6, 5 | still 70%+ down |
| 05:00–05:10 | 12, 19, 20 | recovery begins |
| 05:15+ | 20, 17, 12 | returning to normal |

**Severity metrics:**

| Metric | Baseline (avg Dec 1–3,5–6) | Dec 4 (trough) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| MEV blocks in 03:00–05:00 UTC window | ~545 | **154** | **–72%** |
| MEV blocks in 03:10–03:40 worst 30min | ~120 | **~19** | **–84%** |
| Total daily MEV blocks | ~6,550 | **5,802** | **–11.4%** |
| Total daily blocks (canonical) | ~7,090 | **6,765** | **–4.6%** |
| Orphaned blocks/day | ~17 | **130** | **7.6x normal** |
| Missed slots (25% of slots missed during worst hour vs normal ~2–3) | ~2–3/hr | **~76/hr** | **25x+** |

The relay bids themselves stayed at normal levels throughout (~200+ bids per 10-min window across all relays). The bottleneck was **delivery** — relays accepted bids but circuit breakers prevented them from delivering the winning payload to proposers, causing a surge in locally-built fallback blocks (with many orphaning due to race conditions on recovery).
